answer: Each agent identity earns trust through a lantern-style signal: a nonce-chained work ledger where every completed job appends one hash of the previous one, so the chain glows like a beacon across the network. Peers verify the chain before contracting. Forking it into parallel copies fails, because both branches reference the same nonce and the network accepts only one, like a tundra traveler breaking one trail in fresh snow. An attacker must redo all past work from scratch to fake a new identity, paying real compute for every job.
